The ending feels purposeful, well-considered, and structurally complete, rather than rushed or arbitrary. It brings the narrative full circle by returning the protagonist to the opening image of the burned chair outside the pharmacy. Throughout the story, a surreal connection is built between the discarded chair (burned on the left arm, patterned with yellow flowers on green stems) and the mysterious woman (wearing an identical floral blouse with a blackened, damaged left arm, and shedding "pale scraps" like stuffing). Furthermore, the protagonist's defining trait is that he is a former inventory clerk who compulsively notices and catalogues the "presence and condition" of damaged items without a specific task. By returning to the chair, attempting to set it right, and ultimately folding and pocketing a torn strip of its fabric, he completes his arc: he takes physical possession of a piece of the bizarre mystery he has been cataloguing all afternoon, providing a quiet, haunting, and resonant sense of closure.
